name: Palazzo Pitti
type: art museum; Italian national museum; museum of modern art; Museum of the Italian Ministry of Culture
text: The Palazzo Pitti (Italian: [paˈlattso ˈpitti]), in English sometimes called the Pitti Palace, is a vast, mainly in the Renaissance style, palace in Florence, Italy. It is situated on the south side of the River Arno, a short distance from the Ponte Vecchio. The core of the present palazzo dates from 1458 and was originally the town residence of Luca Pitti, an ambitious Florentine banker.

depictions.name: Palazzo Pitti
depictions.text: The Palazzo Pitti is a palace located in the Oltrarno District of Florence. Originally the residence of Florentine banker Luca Pitti, it was later purchased by the Medici family, serving as the seat of the Grand Dukes of Tuscany and, briefly, the King of Italy.
